text:
carmen: Quickstart node sample behind an ngrok tunnel returns 402 on first call. Using sample-app v0.4 + SDK v1.3.2, REDWOOD_API_KEY set. Locally -> 200, via ngrok -> 402 workspace_payment_required. Anyone seen this?

lee: Are you using a user key or service account? Ngrok can rewrite Host headers which trips our billing proxy.

carmen: It's a user key (Profile -> API keys). Curl to localhost:3000/hello gives 200. Same curl to https://abcd1234.ngrok.io/hello gives 402. Server log shows header x-workspace-id: ws_sundial. SDK logs say first_call_status=blocked_by_payment.

rachel: Can you paste redacted Authorization header and the response body?

carmen: Auth header: `Authorization: Bearer sk_live_REDACTED`. Response: ```HTTP/1.1 402 Payment Required
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":{"code":"workspace_payment_required","message":"Workspace ws_sundial must add billing"}}```

support-bot: Note: INF-482 created - ngrok host header can cause billing proxy origin mismatch.

lee: Workaround: start ngrok with `ngrok http 3000 -host-header=localhost:3000` or ensure X-Forwarded-Host is preserved. That keeps the proxy origin check happy.

carmen: Tried the host-header flag and it fixed it. First call now 200 and sample app proceeds. I'll add a short note to quickstart README about ngrok host headers + check billing CTA.

rachel: Also adding a support-runbook bullet: when users report 402 on quickstarts, ask them to confirm billing status in console and whether they're tunneling via proxies like ngrok.

carmen: Thanks all! :thumbsup:
